planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled or part shade, sheltered from harsh winter wind and hard freezes.

directions: This dramatic New Zealand perennial forms a broad clump of arching, silvery-scaled sword-shaped leaves that catch light beautifully in a woodland-edge or coastal border. It tolerates full sun in cool, humid climates but colors and performs best with afternoon shade in warmer zones, where leaf scorch can occur. Inconspicuous flowers are followed by orange berries on female plants when a male is nearby. Give it sharp drainage, since soggy winter soil is its main limiting factor outside mild coastal gardens.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring in moist, humus-rich, acidic soil under high open-canopy shade, mimicking its native New Zealand beech-forest floor habitat.

directions: Unlike its more sun-exposed relative Astelia chathamica, this species grows naturally as a true forest-floor plant beneath New Zealand native canopy and is genuinely happy in full shade. Bronze-to-olive, finely nerved arching foliage forms a graceful fountain-shaped clump that pairs well with ferns and hostas in a shaded woodland bed. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, and mulch the crown in colder parts of its range to protect it from hard freezes.

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings or plant container-grown shrubs in spring in acidic, humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil under dappled to full woodland shade, sheltered from drying wind.

directions: A true New Zealand forest-understory shrub, mountain horopito thrives in the same deep, cool shade it enjoys beneath native beech and podocarp canopy. Leathery leaves marbled in shades of green, maroon, and cream release a distinctive peppery scent when crushed, and mature plants produce small dark berries. It resents hot afternoon sun and dry soil alike, performing best in a sheltered, humid woodland garden with steady moisture. This is a slow-growing, low-maintenance foliage shrub for shaded borders in mild-winter climates.

subcategory: evergreen coastal perennial with giant glossy leaves

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in rich, moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in part shade with protection from hot midday sun and drying wind, ideally in a cool, humid coastal microclimate.

directions: This striking perennial from New Zealand's remote Chatham Islands produces bold, glossy, ribbed leaves the size of dinner plates topped by dense rounded clusters of vivid blue flowers in late spring. It is notoriously fussy outside cool, humid, maritime climates, demanding constant moisture, rich organic soil, and reliable shade from intense sun. Gardeners in the Pacific Northwest and similar mild coastal zones have the best luck; inland heat and drought quickly cause collapse. Grow it as a specimen in a sheltered shade bed with generous mulch and steady irrigation.
